triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The below-floor half of the South Korea pair (heading 9903.02.80) started at 2026-02-15 instead of at the 2025-11-14 handoff from terminated heading 9903.02.56, so its 15 percent floor top-up was missing for three months.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 5 (kr-79), below-floor sibling: 8 effective_from changes plus one effective_period proof atom per rule quoting the 9903.02.56 compiler's note; module source_verification gains us/statute/hts/9903.02.56 as a second corpus_citation_path. Same indirect-grounding caveat as index 5. No formula change.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff moves versions[0].effective_from from '2026-02-15' to '2025-11-14' on all eight rules of the 9903.02.80 module while leaving every formula, parameter value, import, input, and output byte-identical, so the only meaning change is the version window — squarely wrong_period_or_effective_date. Reading the provision through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, corpus commit d9d6fba0b9) shows 9903.02.80 itself states no effective date, while 9903.02.56 ends with the verbatim string "[Compiler's note: This provision was terminated on November 14, 2025. See 90 Fed. Reg. 55964]" that the new effective_period atoms cite, so the pre-fix February date had no source grounding and the corrected date is anchored to the in-corpus predecessor termination. I could not refute the kind: it is not mechanical (eight effective dates changed, not just excerpts or hashes), not untraceable_branch (a date-specific kind exists and fits better), and not an enhancement (the module already claimed a start date and claimed the wrong one). The sibling 9903.02.79 moves identically, matching the "handoff with no gap" reading.
triage.verifier_notes: Two caveats a reviewer should weigh, neither of which overturns the verdict. (1) Grounding is cross-source inference, not a stated date: the corpus text of us/statute/hts/9903.02.80 carries no effective date, so the corrected 2025-11-14 comes from the predecessor heading 9903.02.56's compiler's-note termination — which is exactly why the module header changed from the singular corpus_citation_path to corpus_citation_paths listing both headings. The commit body is candid about this ("kr-79/80 dates are pinned by the 9903.02.56 compiler's-note termination"), and it is a weaker form of grounding than the Switzerland/Liechtenstein siblings, which cite Annex II of 90 FR 59281 inserting 9903.02.82-.91 effective November 14, 2025 (a range that does not include .79/.80). (2) This is an intra-PR review-round fix: commit 4d2856a958 is dated 2026-08-02 and PR #1197 merged 2026-08-02T18:34Z, so the defective 2026-02-15 date was introduced and corrected within the same PR and never stood on main. If the corpus is meant to hold defects that survived to main, flag this one; if it holds any encoding-vs-source correction, it qualifies. Also note the rest of the diff (proof atoms, plural citation paths, the summary paragraph about the handoff) is provenance/mechanical — the eight date lines are the sole meaning change. The first reader's impact reading checks out arithmetically: 2025-11-14 to 2026-02-15 is three months during which the below-floor 15 percent arm would not have fired, leaving a coverage gap after 9903.02.56 terminated.
